quick.summary: Why correct words can still lose people, and how to explain for the listener.
quick.takeaway: Same facts, their words, what they need first.

beats.line: I explained the delay to sales. Why did they look lost?
Plain is not patronising. Keep the facts, change the words.
Ask first: what will this person do with it?

board.text: what will they do with it?

beats.line: Sales needs to know when they can promise it to clients.
Then lead with that, not the database.
It lands Thursday. You can tell clients today.
Same facts, their words. Nobody looks lost.

quiz.question: You are explaining a technical delay to the sales team. What should you lead with?
options: When they can tell clients it will be ready
The technical cause of the delay
The tools being used to fix it
quiz.explanation: Leading with what the listener will do with the news makes the rest easy to follow.

quiz.question: Using plain words with a non expert audience means leaving out important facts.
quiz.explanation: The facts stay the same; only the words and the order change to fit the listener.
